what: [research-infra][matrix-accuracy] The coverage matrix's bracket_geometry cells for 7 ict_scalp legs (ict_scalp_eth_15m, ict_scalp_sol_15m, ict_scalp_xrp_15m, ict_scalp_xrp_5m -- all execution=live, routed solely to bybit_1; plus ict_scalp_sol_5m, ict_scalp_avax_5m, ict_scalp_5m -- execution=shadow) carried status=pending with a ref explicitly claiming 'this is genuinely pending, not blocked' -- and a companion test (tests/test_rollup_movable_cut.py's test_measured_state_2026_08_17) independently asserted the same: 'bracket_geometry ... HAS a sweep producer of its own ... m20_fleet_exit_sweep.classify returns scalp with a real SCALP_HARNESS. A session can move them.' BOTH WERE WRONG, and both made the identical mistake: they verified classify()/FAMILY_HARNESS maps 'scalp' -> scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py (true), and inferred sweepability from that alone, without checking whether the SWEEP PLANNER actually schedules the family. It does not. e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py::plan_legs restricts its grid to `fam not in ("donchian", "pullback", "squeeze"): skip`, with its own comment: 'scalp/fvg carry a REAL tp_at_r/tp_r bracket rather than the 50.0 sentinel, so this grid would mean something different on them.' VERIFIED by actually running the planner, not by re-reading prose: `python3 scripts/research/e35_shard_plan.py --only ict_scalp_eth_15m,ict_scalp_sol_15m,ict_scalp_xrp_15m,ict_scalp_xrp_5m --ignore-missing-data` returns 0 jobs, all 4 `out_of_scope_family:scalp`. No other sweep tool covers bracket_geometry for this family -- mi312_scalp_target_arms.py exists for the scalp family but answers a different question (MFE/target-setting, not tp_r x atr_stop_mult x timeout geometry). IMPACT: these cells were misclassified as 'MOVABLE BY A SESSION' in scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py's own DONE-CONDITION report (read as 4 movable, real-money-tier work this lane nearly queued a live sweep dispatch against before verifying the planner would actually run it) -- a session trusting that label would have spent real compute dispatching a sweep that structurally cannot produce a result. NOT A LIVE-RISK FINDING: no config was shipped or proposed, no live behavior changes. RESOLUTION NEEDED (not fixed here): either build a bracket-geometry sweep methodology for a real fixed-TP harness (a new tool, not a flag on the existing one -- the grid semantics genuinely differ), or the operator makes an explicit call that bracket_geometry is permanently out of scope for the scalp family and the matrix should read `n/a` rather than `blocked`.
